column1: # tests/memfn/rows.tsv — THE KIT'S ROW MANIFEST ([MEMFN-ROWCON] N4,
# docs/design/memfn/row_contracts.md rev 4.1 §4). HAND-MAINTAINED: one line
# per row of each of the kit's selection tables (the composer's arms,
# memfn/src/compose.c `arms[]`, the run compare's rows, memfn/src/runcmp.c,
# and the offset-skip function's `fn_rows[]`, memfn/src/ofsskip.c, every
# slot; R4e'.0). It is NOT derived from fields.def or from the kit's
# sources: run_rows.sh derives the kit's actual row set independently (an
# MF_TRACE build of the kit prints every row of every table at exit) and
# fails if the two disagree in EITHER direction.
# A row added to the kit adds its line here in the same commit (or the
# check is red); a row deleted deletes its line.
# Columns (TAB-separated; `-` is empty):
#   table      `arms`, `runcmp` or `fn` (the trace's table names)
#   row        the row's name (the trace's `row=`)
#   reach      WHY the row exists, from a CLOSED set:
#                pcrec                    pcrec's corpus reaches it (the census
#                                         floor in row_floors.tsv holds it)
#                total-fallback           the table's last row: chosen only when
#                                         no other row serves a site
#                pending-site:<trigger>   built ahead of the pcrec site that
#                                         will reach it; <trigger> names it
#                contract-reach:<family>  reached only by the kit's contract
#                                         tests; <family> is a G2 family
#                                         (memfn/tests/run_g2.sh FAM_FLOORS)
#              Anything else is refused: a row with no reason is deleted (D77).
#   wkind      `pattern` (a pcrec compile; required for reach=pcrec) or
#              `fixture` (a tests/memfn/arm_fixtures.c fixture; required for
#              every other reach)
#   wflags     pcrec flags for the witness compile (pattern only), space-
#              separated, after `-p rx --features all`
#   witness    the pattern text, or the fixture name
#   signature  a short literal of the ROW'S rendering: it must be in the
#              witness's artifact, and the trace must show the row chosen
#              there. `\n`, `\t` and `\\` are escapes.
#   cflags     pcrec flags for the control compile (pattern only)
#   control    the control: `=` (the witness pattern again, under cflags),
#              another pattern, or another fixture. In the control artifact
#              the row must NOT be chosen and the signature must be ABSENT.
# [REQ-HANDOFF-L1] (abi 75): the two bounded start-scan rows' witnesses add
# `-fno-req-handoff`; their pattern's pre-check handoff otherwise re-enters
# (NEXT's `handoff` row ranks above the start-byte rows).
# [MEMFN] R17-b' B1 (lane fdb1): table `fd`, the finder table (memfn/src/
# finder.c `fd_rows[]`), 19 rows. None is routed at B1, so none renders a
# byte: a `fd` row's "rendering" is the MF_TRACE build's SHADOW record
# (`MFTRACE FD ... row=<id> pick=<form>`), and rows_check.py reads a `fd`
# witness's signature from the fixture's FD records. Every `fd` row's reach is
# `pending-site:<its routing step>` (r17b_prime.md §3.4 [rev3 B7]); a row no
# B1 site can reach (it reads the consumer kind, stated from B2; E, read by no
# row before B3a; H, B9's; a W64 pick, B6's; or B3a's presence facts) has
# witness kind `-` and prints UNREACHED with its step. Each routing step flips
# its rows to `pcrec` with a census floor and a witness. R17-b' B2 (lane fdb2)
# routed D1, D1c and D1w: their reach is `pcrec`, their witness a pattern,
# and their signature is read from the traced compile's `MFTRACE FDROUTE`
# record (row and arm), not the artifact, because a routed row's pick renders
# exactly the text its pre-table arm did (zero movers): the text cannot tell
# the routed decision apart (r17b_prime.md §1.6 [rev3 B5]).
# R7w is `pcrec` too, as the walk's UNROUTED default terminal (lane n2fix):
# from B2 the finder's decision is a live DEFINE-phase selection at every FIND
# site, and R7w is what every site no D1 row claims reads (it returns NULL and
# renders the pre-table arm until B4), so the census chooses it; its signature
# is the `MFTRACE FD` record's, and its control is a one-byte site D1 claims.
# The control is what makes a signature mean something (learnings §3): a
# literal that also appears where the row is not chosen proves nothing.
# run_rows.sh also holds every signature to EVERY artifact it compiled and
# every fixture: wherever the signature appears, the trace must show its row.
